r.Segura/Lucksprings: Folk of Lucksprings were unwilling to trade with the Grendel of Morajasse, whom they associate with Governor Rahab's tyranny.
r.Skallahn/Fareskov: Two thralls, Vigdis and Toki, were murdered in Fareskov last season in a case linked to an eternal interest in its dark forest. The smidr Harald Fourforge suspects the Hungry Beast.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Mentioned in passing: a Karass emissary travelled to Dawnguard to deliver Anka Karass's missive for the Imperial Consul.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: Mentioned in passing: the Karass suggested the wayhouse might be moved to Saltmarsh instead.
r.The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth: Mentioned in passing: the Karass have largely abandoned their villages on the Plains of Teeth, which they suggested as an alternative wayhouse site.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: The Karass want the Last Battle Wayhouse removed from the Untrod Groves, fearing it has woken the Manticore Earl. Replacing it would mean abrogating it and losing its special striding benefits.
r.Zenith/Occursion: Tsark asked to house two sages and their staff at the abandoned Spire of the Night Sun near the border of Occursion as a trial diplomatic post.

Best beware my sting.d: Writing to the Castle of Thorns, the Earl of the Groves voiced 'deep concern' that some in Dawn reject his nobility, and invited sixteen nobles to a feast at the Red Hall, reached by a conjunction during the Autumn summit. Guests are protected by hospitality, but yeofolk are not, apart from the two knights-errant who accepted his test of mettle. He staked his remaining favour, a gift from Penni the White, against the favours taken from him, with Clevis, a herald of Tharim, judging. Yeofolk followers led by Tristan Seneschal planned to attend the Guising Fayre. Hugh de Veran's Throne Room restoration was finished, and the National Assembly may urge him to research Penni the White, the First Empress or another monarch.

n.Dawn: Dawnish nobles were invited to the manticore's feast and wager, and holders of its favours were given the final say over who attends. The National Assembly also had the chance to direct Hugh de Veran's research, perhaps towards how Penni the White avoided the manticore's sting.

t.The Barrens: The self-proclaimed Earl continued to press its claim to Dawnish nobility within the newly conquered Barrens, now hosting a feast for Dawn's nobles on its lands there.

r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: A conjunction was due to open to the Red Hall, the Earl's home in the Untrod Groves, admitting sixteen guests to the feast and wager.

Born with insight.d: Nearly five hundred votes opposed the General Assembly's mandate, many probably from the Wisdom Assembly backing Cardinal Silas of the Cenotaph. The Varushkan Assembly could enact Jaromir Ostrovyn Kostka's call to move against those spreading blasphemy, though Varushkans would then expect their leaders to show no tolerance either. In Wintermark, Rafe's mandate brought rumours that Valdr Grieversonn's family farmstead in Hahnmark bears a strange aura and that he has shown interest in the Sungate. The Assembly could confront or talk to him. Vigilance could urge Varushkan–Wintermark cooperation, and Wisdom could defy the General Assembly at risk of a crisis of faith. Magistrates will ignore Judgement 42 and Nekoda's inquisition proposal.

n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr are named among those who embraced false auras, alongside Highborn and Dawnish.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is named as one of the nations most prone to question the Synod, where the General Assembly's narrowly backed mandate has less effect.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan Assembly could enact a mandate rallying schlacta and wardens to confront false Virtues head-on, though this would create an expectation that Varushkan leaders at Anvil show no tolerance either. The Vigilance Assembly could also urge Varushkans to cooperate with Wintermark against false Virtues.
n.Wintermark: Rafe's mandate urging people to report malign auras to the stormcrows has surfaced suspicions about Valdr Grieversonn, and the Wintermark Assembly must choose whether to confront him or invite him to talk. Wintermark could also be encouraged to join Varushka in a northern bulwark against false Virtues.

t.Hahnmark: A farmstead in Hahnmark, home of the Grieversonn family, is rumoured to bear a strange aura, and Valdr Grieversonn has been seen near the Sungate half a dozen times in six months. The Wintermark Assembly may send magistrates to confront him or seek talks.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Karov is cited as one of the territories where the Firestarters once attacked.

Carved in stone.d: The hallows sworn to by Silas of the Cenotaph and Iniska Ashwood were removed, breaking their oaths, and a doom settled on the Wisdom and Prosperity assemblies. Their preachers became quarrelsome and resentful for a year, though a sincere public oath can lift the curse. Pride was spared, apparently because Zadkiel de Coeurdefer stepped down promptly. Viviane Barossa kept her oath to the end, and Vigilance congregations gained two extra votes. Following complementary judgements by the Wintermark and Loyalty assemblies, the Forge of Bonds could be commissioned at Wood Heath in Hahnmark before the end of Winter 387YE. It would create a Keeper of Oaths to carve one important oath a season into its walls, though some warned that this would make breaking such oaths far more perilous.

n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: in a scop's tale, Gulnar's wife is said to have died long ago fighting the Thule.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark Assembly's judgement helped prompt the proposed Forge of Bonds, an oathing place at the Fingers that echoes the stormcrow's role and that many Wintermarkers feel is right. Some scops, however, warn that carving oaths in stone tempts fate.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark could become the home of the Forge of Bonds, an edifice where a Keeper of Oaths would record important vows, if it is commissioned by Senate motion before the end of Winter 387YE.

r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: The Fingers in Wood Heath, where the formation of Wintermark is celebrated, is the proposed site for the Forge of Bonds. It would cost 11 white granite and 33 crowns in labour, with oaths cut into its white granite walls.

Climb every mountain.d: The Disciples of Sulemaine, cast out when the sword scholars were sundered, hid in heterodox temples in Zenith, rebellious citadels in Cinion and iconoclastic spires in Operus. Herminius' mandate, upheld 234-20, was welcomed by pro-Imperial spires but not by those actually sheltering the Disciples. The Urizen Assembly could pass a mandate (two competing wordings were offered) creating a raiding venture, Drive out the Disciples. Committing a combined strength of at least two thousand would kill dozens and force the Disciples to respond. Such raids would be illegal unless the Senate outlawed membership of the Disciples, letting magistrates lead the raids at no cost to the Senate.

n.The League: Mentioned in passing: rebellious citadels in Cinion shelter the Disciples partly because their people blame the Empire for the League taking the territory.
n.Urizen: Urizen faced the choice of driving the Disciples of Sulemaine out by force, either through illegal raids by its military units urged by a Synod mandate or lawfully alongside magistrates if the Senate outlawed the fraternity, with many sentinels keen to join any such campaign.

t.Morrow: The Disciples were sheltering in iconoclastic spires of Morrow, where Herminius' call to expel them had no effect, making them potential targets of any raids to drive them out.
t.Spiral: Disciples of Sulemaine were found in rebellious Urizeni citadels in Spiral's Cinion region, where resentment of the Empire over the loss of the territory gave them shelter.
t.Zenith: Zenith, home of Senator Herminius, held heterodox temples long sceptical of the Synod that sheltered the Disciples in its high peaks and refused to turn them out.

r.Morrow/Operus: Disciples dwelt in the highest peaks of Operus, in iconoclastic spires where followers of Abraxus seek ways to breach the Labyrinth, and these spires would face raids if Urizen moved to drive them out.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Rebellious citadels in Cinion, whose people blame the Empire for the League's seizure of the territory, sheltered Disciples of Sulemaine.
r.Zenith/Clypion: Clypion's highest peaks were among the places where the Disciples found safe harbour in spires sympathetic to their philosophy, unmoved by Herminius' mandate.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Proceris was among the mountain refuges of the Disciples, sheltered by spires that question the Synod and would not expel them voluntarily.

Construct Adelaarskade.d: The Holberg College of Engineering was called upon to plan the dykes, which were costed at 30 wains of weirwood and 90 crowns in labour and would take three months to build. Once the land was suitable, the Rebeshof Roadwarden, Lia Adelaar van Holberg, was to fund pig markets in the Marches and encourage the Sand Fishers to farm Rebeshof and Utterlund as foreigners. Otmar van Holberg, members of the Kleist von Ennerlund family, Cees Van Holberg, Morlock and others contributed money and weirwood after the Autumn Equinox and Winter Solstice. On completion, the penalty to farms in Holberg would be removed, and a year later both regions would lose their marsh quality.

n.The League: League citizens, led by Otmar von Holberg and the Adelaar family, drove and largely funded a project to make Holberg's marshy land fit for farming.

t.Holberg: Completion of Adelaarskade would remove the penalty affecting farms across Holberg and reshape the landscape of two of its regions.

r.Holberg/Rebeshof: Rebeshof's wetlands were to be drained by the dykes, losing their marsh quality a year after completion, with its Roadwarden pledged to encourage Sand Fishers to farm the land.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Utterlund's wetlands were also to be drained, losing their marsh quality a year after completion and becoming more appealing for farming, including by Sand Fishers.

Construct Bulgakov Memorial.d: Announced in Autumn 387YE, the memorial was designed by Triska Markova of the Druzhba Karova. It required 4 wains of weirwood, 1 wain of white granite and 15 crowns in labour, alongside standard costs, and took three months to build. Triska Markova supplied 1 throne 5 crowns and all of the weirwood and white granite. Rhys Nighthaven and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov each gave 1 crown. All of these contributions were made after the Autumn Equinox. The finished monument takes the form of warding stakes standing around Bulgakov in Duzekani, Karov.

n.Varushka: The memorial honours Varushkan citizens slain by the Cold Sun and the knights-errant who sacrificed themselves to save them, and a Varushkan of the Druzhba Karova designed it and largely paid for it.

t.Karov: Karov gained a completed monument at Bulgakov marking the losses its people suffered in the Cold Sun's attacks.

r.Karov/Duzekani: Warding stakes now stand around Bulgakov in Duzekani, a memorial to the vale's dead and to the knights-errant who held back the scions.

Construct Dancer's Rest.d: Announced at the Autumn Equinox 387YE, the Dancer's Rest was planned as a centre of education and rehabilitation for refugees and ex-slaves, forming part of the Proffered Hand Network, which was to fund it fully. The commission called for 10 wains of weirwood, 30 crowns in labour and three months of work. After the Equinox, Sister Rosa supplied the weirwood and Sufyan i Zuhri i Guerra provided 3 thrones and 6 crowns. The sinecure was completed, and the title of Hand to the Dance became available for the Navarr National Assembly to appoint, with tenure, for the first time at the Winter Solstice 387YE.

n.Navarr: The Navarr National Assembly gained a new tenured title, the Hand to the Dance, which it could appoint for the first time at the Winter Solstice 387YE.

t.Miaren: Miaren became home to the Dancer's Rest, a Navarr-held centre of education and rehabilitation for refugees and former slaves.

r.Miaren/Serenael: The Dancer's Rest was raised at Seren in Serenael, adding a weirwood sinecure that belongs to the Proffered Hand Network.

Construct Forge of Bonds.d: Proposed by the senator for Kallavesa and seconded by the senator for Temeschwar, the motion took up a time-sensitive opportunity described in the Carved in Stone wind of fortune. The Forge of Bonds lets the Keeper of Oaths carve one oath each season into the Fingers through a statement of principle. It cost 11 wains of white granite and 33 crowns in labour, took three months to build and has no upkeep. After the Autumn Equinox, Veikko Bondforger provided 4 thrones, 1 crown and the 11 wains of white granite. With the work complete, the Loyalty Assembly could appoint the first Keeper of Oaths at the Winter Solstice 387YE.

n.Wintermark: The Forge of Bonds now stands in Wintermark's territory of Hahnmark, where one oath each season will be carved into the Fingers.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark gained the Forge of Bonds, built in the Fingers, where the Keeper of Oaths can carve one oath into the stone each season.

r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: The Forge of Bonds was constructed in Wood Heath, and the oaths of the Keeper of Oaths are carved into the Fingers there.

Construct Hounds Hall.d: The motion arose from an opportunity described in the Here comes the night Wind of Fortune. It commissioned the Hounds Hall in Lestasny, Karsk, at a cost of 15 wains of white granite and 45 crowns in labour, with three months needed to complete it. After the Autumn Equinox, Sirka Parakgoosier Bashnya provided 5 thrones, 3 crowns and the full 15 wains of white granite. Anastasiya Lukashovna Volkov contributed a further 2 crowns. Once the hall was finished, the Boyar's Hasta gained the sellsword quality.

n.Varushka: Varushkan citizens funded and supplied the hall, and its completion gave Varushka's new army, the Boyar's Hasta, the sellsword quality.

t.Karsk: Karsk's senator proposed the motion, and the Hounds Hall was raised in Ivarsguard as a base for the Boyar's Hasta.

r.Karsk/Lestasny: The Hounds Hall edifice was built in Lestasny from white granite, and its completion granted the Boyar's Hasta the sellsword quality.

Construct Kennels of Hay.d: Proposed by the senator for Mitwold and seconded by Upwold, the motion created the title of 'Kennelmaster of Hay's Home for Wayward Dogs', a money sinecure in Hay, Mitwold. It cost 10 wains of white granite and 30 crowns in labour and took three months to complete. The Carefoot and Shaw Trading Company undertook to fund it, and after the Autumn Equinox Coal Carefoot provided 3 thrones 6 crowns and the 10 wains of white granite. With the work complete, the Kennelmaster of Hay can be appointed by unanimous decision of the senators of the Marches, for the first time at the Winter Solstice 387YE, and holds the post with tenure.

n.The Marches: The Marches gained a new money sinecure whose holder, the Kennelmaster of Hay, is appointed with tenure by unanimous decision of the Marcher senators. It was proposed by Mitwold's senator, seconded by Upwold's, and funded by Marcher traders Carefoot and Shaw.

t.Mitwold: Mitwold's senator proposed the motion, and the new kennels and their sinecure were built within the territory at Hay.

r.Mitwold/Golden Downs: Golden Downs is where the Kennels of Hay, 'Hay's Home for Wayward Dogs', were built, completed in time for the first Kennelmaster to be appointed at the Winter Solstice 387YE.

Construct Rebellion's Ridge.d: Rebellion's Ridge was commissioned by Alfred Eawulfson in the name of Jedediah Boon, as a memorial for friars and pilgrims studying Pride and as a boost to the territory's congregations. It cost 50 wains of white granite and 150 crowns of labour, plus standard costs, and took three months to build. Eawulfson and Boon supplied most of the resources, with further granite from Charlie Skinner and smaller sums from Farren Silver Streams, Rhys Nighthaven, Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov and Erasmo di Tassato. Contributions came in between Autumn 387YE and Spring 388YE. Once complete, congregations in Mournwold receive two extra doses of liao each season, with the first arriving at the Autumn Equinox 388YE.

n.The Marches: The Marches gained a great work in its territory of Mournwold, a memorial to the Ore Hills Rebellion's leaders that gives the congregations there two extra doses of liao each season.

t.Mournwold: Mournwold's congregations receive two additional doses of liao each season from the Autumn Equinox 388YE, and the territory gains a memorial to Pride for friars and pilgrims to visit.

r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Rebellion's Ridge was raised in Boon County in the Ore Hills, the site of the rebellion whose leaders it honours as exemplars of Pride.

Construct Sorrowful Tunnels.d: The motion followed opportunities described in the Long Shadows and Sorrowful Tunnels Winds of Fortune of the 387YE Summer Solstice. The mine cost 20 wains of weirwood and 60 crowns in labour, and took three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox, Irontide Flax provided 7 thrones, 2 crowns and the 20 wains of weirwood. Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven gave one crown each. The motion stressed that only the upper levels were to be worked. Once the mine was finished, the Sorrowful Tunnels became a bourse resource that the Imperial Senate could allocate.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs' territory of Skarsind gained a new mithril mine, and their senator for Skarsind seconded the motion.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind became home to the Sorrowful Tunnels mithril mine, whose output became a bourse resource for the Senate to allocate.

r.Skarsind/Gildermark: The Sorrowful Tunnels mithril mine was built in Gildermark, with work confined to the upper levels.

Construct Temeschwar Counting House.d: The motion built an edifice in Temeschwar under the Forwards and Rewards Wind of Fortune. It cost 5 wains of weirwood, 5 wains of white granite and 30 crowns in labour, and took three months to complete. Sebastian Adolphus von Temeschwar supplied most of the money along with all the weirwood and one wain of granite. Askien Alanovich Vesimerov and Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar added further crowns. Laughlan Vi Temeschwar provided the remaining four wains of granite after the Winter Solstice. Once complete, the counting house channels donations to the Bloodied Rose in Temeschwar, giving the Virtue Fund an extra 14 crowns each season from the Summer Solstice 388YE.

n.The League: League citizens, chiefly Temeschwar figures such as Sebastian Adolphus von Temeschwar and Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, largely funded and supplied the counting house that now feeds the Virtue Fund.

t.Temeschwar: A new counting house stands in Temeschwar, directing donations to the Bloodied Rose into the Virtue Fund at 14 crowns a season from Summer 388YE.

Construct Temeschwar Superlative Citizen.d: Announced in Autumn 387YE by the Master of Rings, the sinecure cost 10 wains of weirwood and 3 thrones 6 crowns in labour. Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar provided the money after the Autumn Equinox, described as paid for by his ever-increasing debts, and Laughlan Vi Temeschwar supplied the weirwood after the Winter Solstice. The resulting title, the Jewel of Anvil, is auctioned annually on the Imperial Bourse and pays 1 throne, 2 crowns and 16 rings a season from the sale of the distillery's goods. Its holder is charged with performing and promoting brazen acts of Pride, enough to make the eternal Barien admit the Way achieves his ends better than any tools of the realms.

n.The League: League citizens Laughlan Vi Temeschwar and Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar funded and supplied a new Imperial title rooted in Temeschwar, with a remit to showcase Pride to the eternal Barien.

t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar gained a new distillery sinecure whose goods fund the Jewel of Anvil, a title championing the virtue of Pride.

r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: The Temeschwar Superlative Citizen Sinecure distillery was built in Hanuri, and its title was first auctioned at the Spring Equinox 388YE.

Construct Yakholme Grange.d: The motion arose from the opportunity described in the Wild is the Wind wind of fortune. Yakholme Grange required 50 wains of weirwood, 25 wains of white granite and 225 crowns in labour, and took six months to build. Contributions came in over several seasons through Summer 388YE, including money from Ebenezer, Khutulun Hakhandra and Orrick, white granite from Khutulun Hakhandra, and weirwood from Richard Conscience, Watkin and Henry Birchsmith, plus smaller donations. Once complete, the grange would raise the level of investment for farms in Upwold by one, establish Stockland as the Empire's premier cattle market, and increase Faraden trade with the Marches.

n.The Marches: The Marches undertook to fund the grange themselves, and on completion its farmers would gain greater investment and taxation from their farms and increased Faraden trade.

t.Upwold: Upwold's senator proposed the motion, and the completed grange would raise the level of investment for farms throughout the territory by one.

r.Upwold/Stock March: Yakholme Grange was to be built at Stockland in Stock March, set to become the Empire's premier cattle market.

Diadem on my brow.d: Using the Throne's power to address the Empire, Emperor Vesna recalled their promise that the Empire would choose where it fights. They credited the drive for militarisation, which mustered six armies in a year and a half, with making victory possible. The Emperor declared their will to destroy the Druj Empire, conquer its land and liberate its septs. They warned that this would demand hard choices, and pledged that the push east would not leave Imperial homes such as Bregasland or Therunin undefended. The address commended Jaromir Ostrovyn Kostka, the Order of the Golden Pyramid, Vauraus Korppitkotka and several investors in the Imperial budget, and Llewellyn Leafstalker.

n.Druj: The Druj were the explicit target of the address, which called for the destruction of their empire, the conquest of their land and the liberation of their septs.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, but the Emperor cited Bregasland, which they held at the time, as an Imperial home that would not be forgotten.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr are not named, though their territory of Therunin was cited as an Imperial home that would not go undefended.

t.Bregasland: The Emperor named Bregasland, then held by the Jotun, as an Imperial home that would not be forgotten during the push against the Druj.
t.Therunin: The Emperor named Therunin among the Imperial homes in the west and south that would not be left undefended while the Empire turned east.

Drowned in tears.d: Asavea remained at war with the Empire and had sent five warships to support the Grendel, though Lady Madrianna hinted at peace if the missionaries stopped. Asavean priests captured in Oran still awaited a decision from the Freeborn generals. The Senate could fund up to three Ibarian rebel armies, and the Freeborn Assembly could make freeing Ibaria its highest calling. Sumaah accepted Ambassador Accalon's apology, closed the matter of abrasion oil, and offered white granite and medicines for the Brass Coast if Imperial fleets escorted the shipment past Asavean pirates. Sumaah also planned to amend the Liberty Pact, welcomed places at the Zemress Naval Academy, and reported Ser Eddard's safe arrival.

n.Grendel: The Asaveans have deployed five large warships to support the Grendel's war against the Empire and are certain to increase that support if the Empire does not change course.
n.Highguard: Accalon of Highguard, Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic, had their apology accepted, was asked to coordinate the Sumaah gift to the Brass Coast and to liaise on Amika Acciai's cloak, and learned that the schema from Ehud of Reumah's Redoubt was due by the Autumn Equinox.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Dylan of the Thornweaver Striding sent questions about abrasion oil and excommunication, and the Sumaah ambassador answered them.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn generals must decide the fate of the Asavean priests held in Oran, and their Assembly could make aiding Ibaria its highest calling. Sumaah offered granite, Sevensalve and liao to help rebuild Feroz and Madruga if Imperial fleets escorted the shipment.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: League merchants helped Ibarian refugees settle in the Empire, and the Senator for Sarvos invited Sumaah students to the Zemress Naval Academy.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: a Wintermark shaman asked the Sumaah ambassador about the story of their uncle and the condor, and the ambassador had nothing to add.

t.Bay of Catazar: Freeborn fleets were escorting Imperial shipping in the Bay. The Sumaah ambassador warned of an unknowable threat rising in its waters, adding urgency to the Escort the Stone Fleet voyage.
t.Feroz: Asavean priests captured when Oran was taken from the Grendel remain under house arrest there, and the Sumaah aid was meant to heal and rebuild Feroz after the damage done by the Grendel governor.
t.Madruga: Madruga, home of the Zemress Naval Academy, was to receive Sumaah students and, with enough escorts, Sumaah help in securing the territory. There was also talk of a joint venture to restore the Zemress Seminary.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Sarvos invited Sumaah students to the Zemress Naval Academy.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: Freeborn fleets were hunting monsters in the Sea of Snow, an option that would fade if the Assembly made aiding Ibaria its highest calling.

Even darkness must pass.d: Imperial magicians turned a Druj Spring curse into healing waters. The Towerjacks and the Argent Sword broke the Tainted Basilisk's ward and retook Lustri. In the north, Dawnish armies and the Golden Axe drove the god-beast Kroll back into its lake, and the Empire claimed Kroll. Most Druj armies withdrew to the Salt Flats of Sanath, while the Hidden Snake and Poison Crane reinforced the Tower of the Skink in Thornfen. The Winter Sun held off six Druj armies, which are now trapped between Bloodwater Marsh and Lustri. Freed slaves and rebel septs took Nesustak Forest and offered a wary truce. The Empire was offered a chance to seize the Whisperwood, and with it the Sarangrave.

n.Druj: The Druj lost Kroll and the Nesustak Forest, and their northern armies fled to the Salt Flats of Sanath. Six southern armies are trapped near Bloodwater Marsh, and they cling on only at the Tower of the Skink and in Whisperwood.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the six Druj armies came down out of Therunin after ruining the Stork's Gaze, and may try to escape back into Therunin's vallorn.
n.The League: The Towerjacks' engineers unravelled the Tainted Basilisk's trap-ward in Lustri and led the assault that returned the forest to Imperial hands.
n.Urizen: Urizen's spectacular Argent Sword helped retake Lustri, and a Night ward now protects Proceris. The Citadel Guard fought in the north, while a captured sentinel, Corisande, and a lost sentinel turned tortured soul, Flavia, threaten Urizeni lives and armies.
n.Varushka: The Northern Eagle and the Boyar's Hasta fought in the northern push. A former Ossium warden, Dmitriy Innokentievich, has returned as a tortured soul leading Druj against the Northern Eagle.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks who broke the Lustri ward are described as Holberg engineers.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the tortured soul Dmitriy Innokentievich was a native of Ossium who served as a Varushkan warden there.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Most of the defeated Druj armies from the northern Sarangrave withdrew here, harried by Imperial raiders.
t.Sarangrave: No one holds dominion. The Empire controls three regions, the Druj two, the rebels one and the vallorn one, and capturing Whisperwood would give the Empire the territory.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the six southern Druj armies set out from Therunin and might try to escape back into its vallorn.
t.Zenith: Imperial armies retook Druj-held Lustri, and a Night ward shields Proceris from Druj guerrillas. Six trapped Druj armies remain on Zenith's border with the Sarangrave.

r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: The Winter Sun held the marsh against six enchanted Druj armies and pushed them to its edges, where they remain trapped and seeking escape.
r.Sarangrave/Kroll: Dawnish armies and the Golden Axe drove the god-beast Kroll back into its lake, and the Empire claimed the region despite heavy casualties. The Palace of the Sleepers has vanished.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: Rebel former slaves and septs, aided by Irra Harah, overthrew the Druj and claimed the forest, halting the Empire at two-fifths of the way to taking it.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: The Tower of the Skink still holds for the Druj, now reinforced by the Hidden Snake and Poison Crane. It is their last bastion in the Sarangrave.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: The region remains under Imperial control, and its field hospitals receive wounded. Druj guerrillas have ambushed patrols there, including one from the Granite Pillar.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: The Empire is three-fifths of the way to taking it while rebel orcs wage a bloody vendetta against the Druj there. A battle at the Uklead Groves offers the chance to seize the region.
r.Zenith/Lustri: The Towerjacks and the Argent Sword broke the Tainted Basilisk's Spring ward and retook the forest for the Empire.
r.Zenith/Proceris: After the Druj plot to make monsters of its bog octopuses was foiled, a Night ward now hunts down remaining Druj guerrillas in the region.

Expand Pride of Ikka's Tears Autumn 387Y.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by Mournwold, the motion took up an opportunity from the Metal and stone Wind of Fortune. The expansion cost 250 thrones and takes six months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox the money was provided almost entirely by Lumi Warmthbringer and Vauraus Korppitkotka, who each gave 124 thrones 7 crowns, with Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven adding a crown apiece. Once finished, the Pride of Ikka's Tears will produce an additional five wains of mithril each season, while its upkeep rises by two thrones per season.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark's senator for Sermersuaq proposed the motion, and the expanded mine in Wintermark's land will yield five more wains of mithril per season once complete, at two thrones more upkeep.

t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq's senator championed the expansion of the territory's great mithril mine, which will deepen its workings with a new shaft and galleries over six months.

r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: Suaq Fount is home to the Pride of Ikka's Tears, where a deep shaft and new galleries are being dug to raise the mine's mithril output by five wains per season.

Has reared himself a throne.d: Estavus proposed an Office of Fire and Stone at the Crucible of Fate in Iteri, Zenith, and invited Archmage Edmundo to a meeting to settle its purpose. Llofir declined parley, offering whisperspore so a Hallow of the Green World could bypass enmity as a test of trust. Both acts would be crimes. Lashonar offered the Conclave one Caucus Forum meeting, with the Asavean Plenum, the Mallum's inhabitants or a Prince of Jarm. Jaheris could arrange a meeting with the Lady of the Semmerlak, but would not approach Dho'uala until her allegiance was settled. Zakalwe asked whether the Military Council truly sought liberation in the Mallum. A Winter eternal set a midnight parley in the Hall of Worlds.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe cited the Barrens, now part of Dawn with small enclaves for surviving septs, as a warning of supposed liberation becoming conquest.
n.Druj: Zakalwe offered, if the Military Council committed to liberation, an enchantment helping Imperial armies arm the non-Druj peoples of the Mallum and hand them any land taken from the Druj. He also judged that the vast fortress of Cassad Ûln shows how much the Druj fear defeat.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Llofir's herald recalled the eternal tending the ruined and broken in Reikos, a Highborn-held territory.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Office of Fire and Stone resembles a fane, a commission the Empire copied from Jotun techniques for dealing with eternals.
n.Urizen: Estavus proposed an Urizen-sited office whose overseer, the Architect of Hammers, could be either an Urizen title chosen by Tally of the Votes or an Imperial one. The offer answered a message from Vossk of Zenith Ascendant on the Archmage of Autumn's behalf.

t.Forest of Ulnak: Zakalwe said the immense Druj fortress of Cassad Ûln in the north of the forest was built to protect their borders and reveals their fear of defeat.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Llofir's tending of the ruined and broken in Reikos was cited as the model for what it would do if invited in through the Hallow of the Green World.
t.Sarangrave: Lashonar's heralds were nonplussed at the Archmage of Night's suggestion of a grand plan in Sarangrave, saying they had only encouraged communication and delivered a message Imperial magicians had requested over Decius Frostspire's rescue.
t.The Semmerlak: Jaheris could not arrange talks with Dho'uala in the Semmerlak's depths, but offered a meeting with the Lady of the Semmerlak, a Summer witch-knight who loathes the creature. Settling her disputed allegiance is his price for any later parley with Dho'uala.
t.Zenith: The City of Fire and Stone proposed building a permanent Office of Fire and Stone in Zenith, letting heralds of Estavus enter regardless of the eternal's standing with the Conclave, overseen by a new Architect of Hammers.

r.Zenith/Iteri: The proposed Office of Fire and Stone would stand at the Crucible of Fate in Iteri, where the Lady of Hammers already has a significant presence. It would cost white granite, mithril and ilium and take three months to build.

Kingdom by the sea.d: Farsighted offered a Map the Eastern Sea scouting voyage past Druj lands. The greater the strength committed, the more it would reveal, from territory names to Gloomsea's secrets, the Axou coast, Thronaskoni, Skoura, the Cliffs of Vore and rumoured eastern isles. Tempest offered a Raid Asavean Shipping voyage now that the Pax Sarcophan had ended the bounty. A flotilla of 15,000 strength could draw out and sink one great warship such as the Wind Tamer. Raptor offered a Hunt Free Landing Kraken voyage that yields valuable Ambrellic, with Freeborn and corsair fleets favoured. Johann Van Basten offered two crowns a portion for the Ambrellic. All three were opportunities only.

n.Druj: The proposed eastern armada would slip past Druj lands while their attention is on Sarangrave, avoiding battle. It could map their coasts and reveal how the Hathjuk sept supports them.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: sinking an Asavean warship would reduce the naval strength the Asaveans could deploy to help the Grendel.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are listed among those the bravest Asavean merchants sail across the Sea of Storms to trade with.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn fleets would count one rank higher, and corsair fleets two ranks higher, when hunting the juvenile kraken off Free Landing, because they know those treacherous waters best.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Sarcophan trader Johann Van Basten, who offered to buy Ambrellic, was visiting the Alivetti Estates on business.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule, like the Druj, are said to be tight-lipped about what lies beyond the mountains near the Cliffs of Vore.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Bay has already been mapped by the Empire. The young, hungry kraken unleashed in its waters were the quarry of the proposed hunt.
t.Forest of Ulnak: An eastern armada of 5,000 to 10,000 strength could delve into the mist-wreathed, largely unmapped isles of Gloomsea on this territory's coast.
t.Madruga: Shining beacons over Madruga's coast had forced some of the kraken released by the Children of Wrecks into the open, letting fleets hunt them. Others hidden in deep caverns would remain a threat whatever happened.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: With 10,000 to 15,000 strength, the armada could push south past the Salt Flats and chart the coast of the Axou territories beyond.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the Druj focus on Sarangrave is what gave the armada its chance to sail past Druj lands.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: a wealthy Sarcophan trader was visiting the Alivetti Estates on business and offered to buy any Ambrellic gathered.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: the Sea of Snow is noted as already mapped by the Empire and home to massive, mature kraken.

r.Forest of Ulnak/Gloomsea: Gloomsea's misty isles, kept unmapped by the Hathjuk sept, could have most of their secrets uncovered if enough ships joined the voyage. At minimum this would reveal how the Hathjuk support the Druj.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Fleets could spend the season hunting one of the immature kraken released off Free Landing for its prized Ambrellic. The creatures could not be eradicated, however.

Lines of care and sorrow.d: The Brine Turtles, Iron Gulls, Naguerro and Storm Sharks advanced cautiously through Ayereed, enchanted by Sky magic. Heralds from a Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae in Icarion and wolves from a Tomb King citadel in Eoradal, joined by a few mostly Sannite Imperial Orcs, could only delay them. Fleisardh fell within a month, its Brine Turtle sept welcoming the invaders. The Grendel are three-fifths of the way to taking Clisearn and the Fundindelve mithril mine, though the Golden Pyramid grand lodge was completed before the Autumn Equinox. Former Salt Lord Ehsan kept Beoraidh neutral. Losing one more region would leave Mareave under no control.

n.Grendel: Four Grendel armies, enchanted by Sky magic, took Fleisardh and are close to seizing Clisearn, the Fundindelve mithril mine and the newly finished Golden Pyramid grand lodge.
n.Imperial Orcs: A few handfuls of Imperial Orcs, mostly Sannites, fought beside the summoned defenders of their arid territory, knowing they could only delay the Grendel advance.

t.Ayereed: The Grendel armies launched their land offensive against Mareave by marching up through the petrified forest of Ayereed.
t.Mareave: Mareave stays in Imperial hands for now, but with Fleisardh lost and Clisearn under threat, losing one more region would leave it under no control. Because of Beoraidh, the Grendel must hold four regions to claim it outright.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Ehsan's city stayed strictly neutral, offering sanctuary to anyone but sending no soldiers. Its control of the only navigable coastal waters may be what kept navies out of the fighting.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: Fighting rages here and the Grendel are three-fifths of the way to taking the region. The completed grand lodge and the Fundindelve mine are at risk, and wary former Grendel households are increasingly inclined towards the Empire.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: A basalt citadel of the Tomb King rose in the shadow of the aqueduct, sending pale wolves to fight the Grendel in Fleisardh.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: The Grendel seized the region with the full cooperation of the Brine Turtle sept, which welcomed the returning armies with open arms.
r.Mareave/Icarion: A Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae here sent its orc-like heralds charging south to meet the invaders and slow their advance.

My passions from a common spring.d: The Commonwealth paid in goods for Imperial crystal mana and offered another 200-mana deal. It declined the covenstone and runesmith proposals and was irritated that Axos had called a Liberty Pact meeting. It offered Imperial admirals study at the Academy of the Cresting Wave for 50 thrones. Doktor Kunz of the University of Volkavaar sought a sungold tablet from the Advisor on the Vallorn, offering future help in exchange. Jarm flatly refused to prove anything to the Liberty Pact. Prince Mila had the Jarmish client nation Zemelslo open its port of Radosmo to Imperial traders, prompting an administrative Senate motion on whether trading there was lawful.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Therunin is referred to as a territory still to be liberated from the Druj.
n.Highguard: The Highborn's wish for dialogue with the Commonwealth on military doctrine, trade and philosophy was welcomed cautiously. The Militärattache suggested they use die Beurteilung to appraise how closer ties might be built.
n.Navarr: Nathair Autumngale, the Advisor on the Vallorn, hosted Commonwealth scholars at the Great Library of Hacynian and set a price for its cracked sungold tablet. The University of Volkavaar accepted that price, offering expertise to help restore Therunin and first access to any discoveries from the tablet.
n.The League: Professor Gelberg's team completed an examination relating to sieges in Holberg. The Commonwealth turned down the Ambassador's offer of places at the Zemress Naval Academy.
n.Wintermark: Finn Pridetalker of Wintermark, Ambassador to the Commonwealth, was thanked for the mana deal and secured another offer. However, Commonwealth crafters refused to share their runesmithing knowledge, and the Militärattache offered apologies to Stormcrow Cynerik of Grayholm Hall for having only limited knowledge of funerary rites.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Professor Gelberg and his scholars had recently completed an examination relating to sieges in Holberg.
t.Therunin: If the sungold tablet is handed over, the University of Volkavaar promises to send experts to help appraise how Therunin might be restored once it is liberated from the Druj, whenever the Ambassador asks.

Ratify Axos Treaty Autumn 387YE.d: Proposed by the senator for Weirwater and seconded by the senator for Madruga, the motion ratified a seven-point treaty. Axos would commit its army, the Shield of Ipotavo, to aid the military conquest of the Sarangrave in line with the Military Council's strategy. The Empire accepted Axos's claim over Thornfen and ceded any claim to it, while Axos agreed not to impede Imperial forces passing through the Sarangrave, including Thornfen. Axos also committed to the safety of the Bloodwater Spears, Waterwalkers and Free People of Sarangrave, including those in Sephals, with the Empire as mediator in disputes. The Empire may hire further Axou military aid, and Axos is to be approached when the Empire moves on the Salt Flats of Sanath.

n.Druj: The Druj, who held the Sarangrave and the Salt Flats of Sanath, faced the prospect of an Axou army, the Shield of Ipotavo, joining the Imperial campaign against them.

t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The treaty provides that Axos is to be approached about further cooperation when the Empire looks to make an incursion into the Druj-held Salt Flats of Sanath.
t.Sarangrave: The Druj-held Sarangrave became the target of a joint campaign, with Axos committing the Shield of Ipotavo to its conquest and promising free passage to Imperial forces and safety for the Bloodwater Spears, Waterwalkers and Free People there.

r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: The Empire accepted the Axou claim to Thornfen and ceded its own, while Axos agreed to let Imperial forces pass through it and to protect the people living in Sephals.

Rebuild First Voice Glade.d: Announced in Autumn 387YE, the commission would rebuild the corpse glade and school of the great bard Gerallt Brackensong. The site had already been consecrated with true liao after a Synod writ of consecration and mandate. The work cost 30 wains of weirwood and 90 crowns in labour, took three months, and was self-funded by a union of bards from across the Empire. It was meant to inspire pilgrims to learn Navarr song and storytelling and to develop their own nations' musical and literary cultures. After the Autumn Equinox, members of the Splitroot and others supplied the full 30 wains of weirwood, plus money including 11 thrones from Nemae Splitroot. No outcome is recorded.

n.Navarr: The project honours the Navarr bard Gerallt Brackensong and promotes Navarr traditions of song and storytelling, and it was announced and largely supplied by Navarr of the Splitroot.

t.Miaren: Miaren was to gain a rebuilt glade and school dedicated to Gerallt Brackensong, intended to draw pilgrims seeking inspiration in the performing arts.

r.Miaren/Oakways: The ruined First Voice Glade and School in Oakways, already consecrated with true liao, was the site chosen for rebuilding as a place of pilgrimage.

Repair Berechiah's Basilica.d: The motion drew on a civil service report from before Winter Solstice 385YE and the Knocking on every door wind of fortune. It created a sinecure costing 10 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood, 45 crowns in labour and three months of work. The Custodes Clavium undertook to cover construction costs and gave 5 thrones 5 crowns after Autumn Equinox 387YE. Cyrus of Athaliah's Handiwork supplied the white granite in two loads of 5 wains, and Merari Navigators of Virtue supplied the 5 wains of weirwood across Spring and Summer 388YE. Once complete, the work creates a title to be appointed by the Vigilance Assembly.

n.Highguard: Highguard benefactors carried the restoration: the Custodes Clavium covered the costs, Cyrus of Athaliah's Handiwork gave the white granite and Merari Navigators of Virtue gave the weirwood, all for a basilica in a Highborn territory.

t.Bastion: Berechiah's Basilica in Bastion was to be repaired as a rallying point for the vigilant against foreign threats, and the motion was proposed by Bastion's own senator.

Repair Celesti Lighthouse.d: Proposed by the senator for Feroz and seconded by Segura, the motion restored the lighthouse according to Eilian Sweetwater's Summer 387YE appraisal, returning it to the care of the Celesti Lighthouse Keeper. It cost 16 wains of mithril, 10 rings of ilium, 60 ingots of weltsilver, 40 ingots of tempest jade and 48 crowns in labour, taking three months. Manolo i Erigo, Bakar i Riqueza, Estevanico i Hayim i Riqueza and Iago i Guerra supplied the materials and money. Once complete, Brass Coast senators could again appoint the Keeper, the Escort Imperial Shipping voyage was replaced with Patrol the Bay of Catazar, and the Senate could restore the Broken Shore Bounty.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page and is linked only because it held part of Feroz that season.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast citizens funded the restoration themselves, and the nation's senators regained the right to appoint the Celesti Lighthouse Keeper.

t.Bay of Catazar: The completed lighthouse replaced the Escort Imperial Shipping voyage with a new Patrol the Bay of Catazar voyage on these waters.
t.Feroz: The Celesti Lighthouse in Feroz was rebuilt with a watchstone lamp. The territory's senator proposed the motion.

r.Feroz/Oranseri: The restored Celesti Lighthouse stands in Oranseri, where it was rebuilt to its former glory with a magically infused watchstone lamp.

So our path is laid.d: After Imperial heroes dismissed the Burhfæst at Graven Rock, the Ice Fishers lost their magical citadel but may build a mundane fort. Under Idun Yrsasdóttir, the Lion of the North hunted the Strong Reeds while the Tower of the North and Fist of Ulven secured the fens. Captured Ottery smugglers betrayed the resistance network, exposing supply drops and safe houses. Jotun raids into Mitwold were held off by four armies. The Strong Reeds now face 1,000 casualties if they leave, or 500 per season if they keep lying low. At Leakey Moss the Empire could seize Jotun orders, hold the standing stones, or kill Eisa Winterborn.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: legend holds that the standing stones at Leakey Moss have stood since the first yeofolk marched to Bregasland from Dawn.
n.Jotun: Jotun armies held Bregasland and, led by Queen Yrsa's daughter Idun with hunters from Tromsa and Raðljóst from Skallahn, began dismantling the Strong Reeds' support network. Meanwhile King Gudmundr and the Queen were both unusually absent from their armies.
n.The League: A significant number of League soldiers, several from Holberg, joined the roughly twenty Imperial warbands helping keep the Strong Reeds hidden and supplied.
n.The Marches: Bregasland remained under Jotun thralldom and the Strong Reeds were left in a perilous position, facing heavy losses whether they leave, lie low or rise. The Marcher Assembly unanimously urged the Bregas to shelter and aid their army.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Eisa Winterborn is noted as having fought the Empire during the earlier campaign in Sermersuaq.

t.Bregasland: The Jotun kept control of the territory, with its people as thralls, while the Strong Reeds' hidden network was exposed through raids, arrests and a smuggler's confession.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: several League soldiers supporting the Strong Reeds came from Holberg and were used to fighting in marshes.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: the Lion of the North was noted to have previously torn apart the old Imperial spy network in Hordalant.
t.Mitwold: Jotun warbands under Eisa Winterborn and Yanya Uranduln raided across the border, but the four armies present prevented any significant damage or loss of wealth. The raids also helped the Jotun identify the Strong Reeds' smuggling routes.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: Seeker Alma, one of the Jotun leaders carrying orders at Leakey Moss, is a tracker from the plains of Reinos.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Eisa Winterborn is noted as having fought during the campaign in Sermersuaq.
t.Skallahn: Veteran Raðljóst from Skallahn were summoned to Bregasland and their scouting proved key to exposing the Strong Reeds. Eisa Winterborn, a prominent yegarra leader from Skallahn, led arrests across the east of Bregasland.
t.Tromsa: Seasoned hunters from Tromsa answered the Queen's call, and their expertise repeatedly forced the Strong Reeds to abandon their positions.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: The Burhfæst anchored to Graven Rock was not renewed and returned to the Summer realm, though there are signs the Ice Fishers of Ldansk may be preparing to build a mundane fortification there.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: A Jotun muster of jarls and Ulfur hunters at Leakey Moss, site of three legendary standing stones, became the target of an Imperial battle opportunity during the Autumn Equinox.
r.Mitwold/Meade March: Jotun warbands raided into southern Meade March but never approached the city of Meade, and the defending armies prevented significant damage.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: Jotun raids struck Oddmire, and without the armies present the warbands might have seriously threatened the people of Odd's End.

Songs like trees.d: The vallorn, roused by Druj magic, was drawn away from the Upper Tarn Valley towards the Imperial armies and was stopped in Peakedge Song. The untested Winter ritual Why Sulemaine Walked Away From The Baker protected the soldiers from Green Lung and greatly reduced their losses. The Druj had also cast a curse akin to Thunderous Tread of the Trees. Ossegrahn's herald explained that the Conclave had failed him, so he had withdrawn and would offer no more boons. He left an enchanted grove where Peakedge Stead stood. The Houses of Healing and Stones from Blood were destroyed. Therunin remains nominally Druj, with the Empire about a fifth of the way to reclaiming Peakedge Song. Wards on the Thorn Guardians and poisoning ettercap nests were offered as opportunities.

n.Dawn: The Golden Sun returned from Astolat to fight the vallorn in Peakedge Song, Dawnish captains marched alongside it, and Dawnish enchanters identified heralds of Woodwyf among the vallornspawn, prompting a Dawnish and League cadre of monster hunters to hunt them.
n.Druj: The Druj burned Peakedge Stead once Lord Rain's protection lapsed and cast a tree-animating curse over Therunin, which they still nominally hold. Their remaining forces appear concentrated in the east, leaving only guerrillas and traps in Peakedge Song.
n.Highguard: Highborn captains joined the campaign, and the priests of Reikos blessed and anointed the soldiers on Chalcis Mount, with some choosing to march with the armies against the vallorn.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War had been recovering from campaigning against the Jotun in the west before this deployment.
n.Navarr: Navarr thorns and brands made up most of the captains fighting in Therunin, but their ancient Peakedge Stead was burned and the Houses of Healing and Stones from Blood were lost. Ossegrahn has withdrawn his support from Greenwatch, and Thornsong House is hidden by Night magic only until the Winter Solstice.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War marched out of Urizen's Morrow, where they had earlier helped the Urizen root out vallorn harbingers probing Peregro.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark captains were among the warbands well represented alongside the two armies.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Sun had been recovering in Astolat since its retreat from Therunin and marched out from there.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War set out from Morrow after six months of furlough there.
t.Reikos: Reikos served as the mustering ground where the Golden Sun, the Wolves of War and the independent captains joined forces before crossing into Therunin. The burning across the border brought home how close the vallorn threat now lies.
t.Therunin: The vallorn was prevented from claiming any further land in Therunin, but the territory remains nominally Druj and is plagued by animated plant life. Peakedge Stead has been destroyed, and an enchanted grove now stands in its place.

r.Morrow/Peregro: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War had helped the people of Urizen root out vallorn harbingers probing Peregro's defences.
r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: The armies gathered at High Chalcis, where priests offered dedication and anointing on the eve of the march. Some Highborn reflected uneasily on how short the distance is between the Gardens of High Chalcis and Therunin.
r.Therunin/Greenheart: Mentioned in passing: the Druj-roused vallorn had spilled out beyond Sweetglades and the Greenheart.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named directly, though the Druj fled east towards the Tarn Valley and their remaining forces in Therunin seem concentrated in the east.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: The vallorn was halted here after relentless fighting, and the Empire is about a fifth of the way to reclaiming the region. Peakedge Stead was burned, and the Thorn Guardians and an ettercap hive at Thorngroves offer chances to weaken the vallorn.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: The vallorn surged out of Sweetglades, and ettercaps migrated from hives at its heart. Two nests found there, in the Squamous Woods and the Twitching Grove, could be poisoned to reduce the vallorn's strength.
r.Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley: The vallorn had seemed set on devouring the Upper Tarn Valley, but it was drawn away towards the Imperial armies instead. The Druj who burned Peakedge Stead left on a trail heading north-east towards the valley.

Stand amid the roar.d: Under Determination of Ice Kaisa, the Narwhal's Spear broke the Cult's strongholds with few casualties and ended its plans to raise an army. The Sun Chamber located all four obelisks, in Tanikipari, Suaq Fount, Suaq Wastes and the Thule-held Silver Peaks, and recovered a coded message. Highborn inquisitors learned that the Cult meant to make Sermersuaq as savage as the Claw. Destroying one obelisk limits the curse to regions that still hold one. Destroying all four ends it. Corrin Arrowsbane, the Sun Chamber's Counsel Zoria and Speaker Nicodemus were each charged with destroying a pillar and slaying its Voice. The Thule said the Dragons would attend to the fourth.

n.Highguard: Highborn pilgrims answering Destin of the Woodwych Harts went north, and their inquisitors exposed the Cult's plan. A Highborn band failed to reach Suaq Fount, so the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly, Nicodemus of Balthazar's Vineyard, is now charged with destroying that pillar.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the page recalls that the Jotun not long ago stormed through Sermersuaq.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Megaris of the Empty Sword, a keen-eyed young sentinel from Spiral, spotted the first obelisk for the Sun Chamber.
n.Thule: Thule warlocks investigating feral beasts and curse wars examined the fourth obelisk in the Silver Peaks alongside Sun Chamber scouts. They said the Dragons would attend to it, without clearly promising to destroy it.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Narwhal's Spear returned home and shattered the Cult while trying to spare its misguided kin. The Winterfolk of Sermersuaq hunted out cultists, and Corrin Arrowsbane is tasked with destroying the Tanikipari pillar.

t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the coded message was found on the body of one of the Chosen, a merchant originally from Kallavesa.
t.Sermersuaq: The Cult's army was broken across the territory, but four buried obelisks threaten to curse Sermersuaq with the savagery of the Claw at the Equinox unless they are destroyed.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Megaris of the Empty Sword, who found the first obelisk, is a sentinel from Spiral.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: the Suaq Wastes obelisk lies close to the border with Tromsa.

r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The fourth obelisk stands here in Thule-held land near the Stonefield Ice Caves. The Thule warlocks investigating it have promised only that the Dragons will attend to it.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: An obelisk guarded by the Voice of the Fount stands here, where cultists sought to disrupt the Pride of Ikka's Tears and seize its mithril. Its destruction now falls to the Speaker of the Highborn Assembly.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Cultists rallied around the Voice of the Wastes guard an obelisk here, and the Counsel of the Sun Chamber, Zoria, is responsible for destroying it and slaying the Voice.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: The first obelisk was found buried near Ittanpari. After Merewalh the Fox's band was driven back, Corrin Arrowsbane is asked to destroy it and kill the Voice of Tanikipari.

The moth for the star.d: Day-magic divinations had spread the names of individual stars across the Empire, though Tacita of Zenith's Twisted Chambers disputed them. Since the Summer Solstice astronomantic rituals had felt heavy and draining, and alignment with tulpas was stronger. The Claw's power to empower violent rituals with blood, interdicted by Lights Aliss, now also extended to the empower spell. The Great Wyrm–Mountain conjunction had ended, but a new one with the Drowned Shepherd meant personal-curse arcane projections would be permanently defunct after the Equinox. Pseudo-constellations appeared over Karov, Hahnmark, Holberg, Spiral and Semmerholm. The Eye of the Heavens observatory was proposed for Mount Polus, and the Pilgrim Flame was expected to return to Anvil.

n.Dawn: The Bondring rose over Semmerholm, stirring thoughts of love and an urge to help others strengthen their bonds, though it had only a limited impact on the people there.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Woven Banner pseudo-constellation recorded last season over Necropolis is noted, its influence now faded.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Trident pseudo-constellation recorded last season over Skarsind is noted, its influence now faded.
n.The League: League presses spread sensationalist copies of the star-name pamphlets, and new night stars appeared over Holberg (the Looking Glass, inspiring reinvention) and Spiral (the Mask, inspiring false personas), while Tassato's Golden Ferret faded.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Serpent Sheds its Skin pseudo-constellation recorded last season over Mournwold is noted, its influence now faded.
n.Urizen: Urizeni scholars were at the heart of the debate: Spider's Vantage spread the first star-name pamphlets, the Twisted Chambers disputed them, the Spire of Shadowed Glass catalogued the night stars, and the Eye of the Heavens observatory was proposed for Mount Polus in Zenith.
n.Varushka: The Paired Dancers appeared over Karov, inspiring a rash of ill-considered romances, several weddings and one memorable fight.
n.Wintermark: The Crab appeared over Hahnmark, prompting inventive thinking and the questioning of established beliefs, coinciding with increased criticism of the Imperial Synod.

t.Hahnmark: The Crab pseudo-constellation was seen in Hahnmark's veiled skies, encouraging people to dwell on past choices and propose seemingly unworkable solutions.
t.Holberg: The Looking Glass rose over Holberg, driving some to abandon their lives for new paths, including a merchant-prince who gave away their wealth to become an artist in the Sumaah Republic.
t.Karov: The Paired Dancers over Karov made it easy to see the best in others, sparking hasty romances, weddings and a brawl.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Serpent Sheds its Skin was recorded here last season, but its influence over sleepers has faded.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the Woven Banner was recorded here last season, but its influence over sleepers has faded.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Spider's Vantage Spire in Redoubt helped circulate the first scholarly pamphlets on the names of the stars.
t.Semmerholm: The Bondring appeared over Semmerholm, inclining people to reflect on love and help others' connections, though visiting Urizen found little obviously changed.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Trident was recorded here last season, but its influence over sleepers has faded.
t.Spiral: The Mask appeared over Spiral, encouraging deception and false personas, though it was largely overshadowed by everything else happening in the territory.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Ferret was recorded here last season, but its influence over sleepers has faded.
t.Zenith: Tacita of the Twisted Chambers, an old Zenith spire, argued the star names were artefacts of the ritual used, while the Eye of the Heavens observatory was proposed for Mount Polus in the territory.

r.Zenith/Occursion: The Eye of the Heavens observatory was offered as an opportunity in Occursion, costing 30 mithril, 20 white granite, 10 weirwood and 225 thrones over two seasons; it would found a new spire and a centre for astronomancy, with the offer ending after the Spring Equinox 388YE.

Those that break a thing.d: The Gathered Storm, swollen with pirates, the fallen corsairs of Isidore i Boyaga, the Navarr traitors of Liath's Blade and a dozen escaped Iron Confederacy ships led by Suranni servants of Dumon, struck Trivento by sea and land. Fighting reached the streets, and the College of the Liberated came under attack. The Red Wind Corsairs, caught part-way through taking to the sea, harried the pirates and were joined by Sarcophan ships from the Alivetti Estates. The attackers fled west, probably towards Madruga or Feroz, having done only minor damage. Afterwards, wrecker gangs accompanied by heralds of Siakha landed to threaten regiones in Sarvos and Necropolis, and Mawrig's Point in Madruga.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: former Grendel vessels sailed with the Gathered Storm, and the newly seaborne Red Wind Corsairs are said to be ready to face the Grendel.
n.Highguard: A wrecker gang landed east of Crown's Quay, butchered a merchant bound for Sanctuary and made for the Stone of Suffering, apparently to curse Necropolis. The Champion of Loyalty, Talos, was asked to stop them.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the traitors of Liath's Blade blamed the Empire for failing to recover Liathaven from the Jotun.
n.Navarr: The traitorous false-steading Liath's Blade, under Captain Ioan Bloodstride, led the bloody fighting in Trivento's streets. They claimed they were angered by the Empire's failure to recover Liathaven, but they seemed just as eager to plunder.
n.The Brass Coast: The Red Wind Corsairs, built around three flagships and rallying corsair family vessels, were decisive in saving Trivento and routed the renegade corsairs of Isidore i Boyaga. They lost several ships and crews, but are now a navy.
n.The League: League soldiers fought in Trivento's streets to protect Sarvos's second city, while the Great Chain and Our Lady of Pride held. The raid did only minor damage and had no real effect on taxation.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs marched to Sarvos from Mitwold after the Summer Solstice.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Children of Wrecks gathered pirates and raiders from across the Bay into their armada. The Red Wind Corsairs, now a navy, can reach any port on the Bay to pursue them or face the Grendel.
t.Feroz: Many Red Wind corsair families come from Feroz, now held by the Children of Wrecks, and the defeated Gathered Storm is thought to be retreating west towards bases in Madruga or Feroz.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Liath's Blade invoked the Empire's failure to retake Liathaven from the Jotun in their battle-cries.
t.Madruga: The servants of Siakha occupy Atalaya, and the Gathered Storm may be retreating there. A wrecker gang also landed near Meceares and camped at Mawrig's Point, and the Champion of Vigilance, Jared, was asked to stop them.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs set out from Mitwold to march to Sarvos.
t.Necropolis: Wreckers landed east of Crown's Quay, left a trail of destruction and headed for the Stone of Suffering, a Winter regio, probably to curse the territory. Talos, the Champion of Loyalty, was asked to stop them.
t.Sarvos: Trivento was attacked from sea and land, with fighting in its streets and at the College of the Liberated, but the defenders drove the raiders off with little damage. Wreckers then landed near Glass Point seeking the Circle of Savagery, and the Champion of Prosperity, Tom Appleseed, was asked to stop them.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Mentioned in passing: the curses of Siakha have cut the Cazar Straits off from the Coast with churning seas and monsters.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: The village of Meceares raised the alarm and warned villages deeper in Calvos Sound when wrecker sails appeared. The wreckers landed out of sight and were later found camped around Mawrig's Point.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Mentioned in passing: the islands of Free Landing are isolated from the Coast by Siakha's curses.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: Trivento was assailed from the sea and from the east, its harbour chain was attacked by carcharadon, and fighting spread through its streets as raiders tried to loot Bocche's wealth. The defenders drove them off with only minor damage.
r.Sarvos/Uccelini: Some wrecker ships slipped through the eastern isles of Uccelini and landed near Glass Point. They were bound for the Circle of Savagery, apparently to curse Sarvos.

Threats that are to come.d: Commissioned by Lula, Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund and Cees van Holberg, Gelberg found Holberg well supplied by imports from Dawn, so the benefits are mostly for the future. The Seven Stores, in Holfried, would drill three deep wells and build seven food stores. They would protect the city against a siege for two seasons, feed any number of refugees and keep one sheltering army in supply. An option would subsidise food for the poor. The Seven Dykes would revive old civil service plans to drain Rebeshof and Utterlund and end the farm penalty in Holberg. A further amendment, the Seven Farms, would persuade the Sand Fishers to raise Marcher pigs there as foreign owners. That would raise taxes by up to six thrones and modestly increase League army supply. All three remain proposals.

n.Dawn: Holberg currently relies on Dawnish yeofolk and Semmerholm merchants for much of its food. Dawn's Estmure, guarded by the Adamant Gate, keeps open the mountain pass that makes any siege of Holberg fail.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: their thirty-year campaign failed to close the Estmure pass, and their destruction of Holberg's dykes let the marshes return.
n.The League: The League could fund siege stores, wells and drainage for Holberg, and court the Sand Fishers as pig farmers. Doing so would boost taxes and League army supply, though not by enough to raise a fourth army.

t.Holberg: Holberg was offered wells and seven grain stores to withstand a two-season siege and feed any number of refugees. It was also offered the Seven Dykes to end its farming penalty and drain marshland for new farms.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm's merchants help feed Holberg. Its Estmure pass and the Adamant Gate form the main barrier any besieger would need to break before starving Holberg.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Mentioned in passing: listed among the marshlands whose draining would most obviously improve Holberg's food supply, though the Seven Dykes proposal drains only Rebeshof and Utterlund.
r.Holberg/Holfried: The proposed Seven Stores edifice, with three deep wells and seven Virtue-named food stores, would be built in hilly Holfried, where the city abuts Estmure's mountains.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: An enemy holding Holmauer and Rebeshof could cut the city's supply lines. The proposed stores would let refugees in Holmauer be fed without starvation.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Sand Fishers practise subsistence fishing and gathering in Misericorde. The appraisal suggests they might expand from there into large pig farms on drained neighbouring land.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: The Seven Dykes would drain Rebeshof, removing its marsh quality a year after completion. The Seven Farms idea would then see Sand Fisher pig farms established there. Its loss to an enemy would help cut the city's supply.
r.Holberg/The Morass: Mentioned in passing: named among the drowned marshes whose draining would improve food supply, but it is not part of the Seven Dykes proposal.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: The League Assembly urged making Utterlund more productive. The Seven Dykes would drain it within a year of completion, opening it to Sand Fisher pig farms as foreign-owned land.

To ruin.d: The Grendel landed three armies at Elos with Asavean support, took the port, then spread across Naris and came seven-tenths of the way to taking Siluri. They plundered crystal mana and valuables and seized the Great Harbour and the Tower of Light and Shadow. The Fist of the Mountains arrived unexpectedly and slowed the invaders, letting most Urizen and their libraries escape. It then fought back into Elos, where a Wintermark warrior shattered the catastrophe sphere, but the army was disbanded. A thousand freed Winter husks now roam Naris, and Eilian Sweetwater is missing. The harbour, docks and tower face ruin by Winter unless the Empire answers. An equinox battle opportunity was offered.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Fist's general had planned to unleash the husks in the Sarangrave, and Redoubt's people wonder whether armies can be spared from the eastern front against the Druj.
n.Grendel: The Grendel took Elos, Naris, the Great Harbour and the Tower of Light and Shadow, looting great wealth, but lost hundreds of mercenaries and their stolen sphere. Their Moridun forces are now quarrelling over the blame.
n.Highguard: The Grendel meant to stop Highguard or Urizen raising navies at Elos, and their sphere might have threatened the Necropolis just across the Couros before it was shattered.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the mountains of Skarsind are named among the places where the Fist of the Mountains learned to fight.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Fist's Winter dead are recalled as having fought in Reinos.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Fist had liberated Madruga and fought in the Quiet Grasses before marching to Redoubt.
n.The League: Tassatan dead walk among the freed husks, and their families seek the return of their burial jewellery. A Grendel maistir hopes League companies will help her defect and settle in Sarvos.
n.Urizen: Urizen lost Elos, Naris and the Tower of Light and Shadow and is close to losing Siluri, and suffered a costly raid. Most of its people and spire libraries were saved by Wintermark's sacrifice.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's eldest army, the Fist of the Mountains, was destroyed saving Elos from devastation. Its founding relic, Pinnacle, was looted by the Grendel and can be recovered on the battlefield.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Grendel intended the destruction of Elos to show that they alone own the Bay, and the missing Eilian Sweetwater may be stranded on a rock somewhere in its waters.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the would-be defector Muirgheal Cuindlis once had links to Feroz under Governor Rahab's occupation.
t.Hahnmark: The lost Fist trained in Hahnmark's mountains, and its relic Pinnacle came from there by tradition. Survivors hope to return it to the summit of the Fingers.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: songs of the fallen Fist of the Mountains will be sung in Kallavesa.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the Fist had liberated Madruga before its long march, and the Grendel's earlier attack on Elos came on their way from Madruga.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: news of a Grendel advance in Mareave adds to the fear in Redoubt.
t.Necropolis: The Fist marched through under disapproving eyes, and the Grendel sphere might have reached the Necropolis had it been set off.
t.Raineach: Mentioned in passing: the tempest jade sphere was taken from the Temple of Tempest Jade in Raineach.
t.Redoubt: Grendel and Asavean forces took Naris, including Elos, the Great Harbour and the Tower of Light and Shadow, and press on Siluri. These sites face ruin by Winter unless the Empire answers.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the Fist and its Winter dead are recalled as having fought in Reinos.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the Fist's general had planned to unleash the Winter husks in the Sarangrave.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the Fist marched through Sarvos, a raid there is reported, and the defector Cuindlis hopes to settle in the city.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the Fist learned mountain fighting in Sermersuaq, where its fall will be sung.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind's mountains are named among the Fist's old battlegrounds.
t.Tassato: Tassato's dead, raised by the Fist's ritual, still carry their burial finery. A merchant prince will reward those who recover it from the husks.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: unliving horrors still linger in parts of Zenith from an earlier use of the ritual, and former Zenith refugees fear a repeat.

r.Madruga/Quiet Grasses: Mentioned in passing: the Fist's Winter dead are recalled as having fought in the Quiet Grasses.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Naris fell entirely to the Grendel, with Elos, its harbour and the Tower of Light and Shadow. A thousand Winter husks now roam the region, and Grendel Sky ritualists seek the hidden tower.
r.Redoubt/Optarion: Mentioned in passing: Optarion is not named on the page; it is touched only by the wider Grendel assault on Redoubt.
r.Redoubt/Siluri: The Grendel are seven-tenths of the way to conquering Siluri and threaten its Academy of Arms, though the shrine to Adelmar the Lion is still in Imperial hands.
r.Redoubt/Tomari: Mentioned in passing: the armada swept around Tomari's headlands on its way to Elos.

Troop of echoes.d: After the revocation and condemnation of Ambassador Fintan Nighthaven, The Flame of Riqueza became Ambassador to Axos. Axos's new envoy, Ilarch Kario Skopos, arranged a ceremonial delegation to the Senate. He also hoped to discuss joint action against the Druj Tower of the Skink and the Liberty Pact. Axos will host a Pact meeting through the Midnight Owl's Caucus Forum to repeal the 384YE Jarm embargo amendment. The Unified Convocation named Fintan an "Enemy of the Creator", and the General Assembly could still vindicate him before his trial. Kantor now offers tomb dust and Masks of the Citadel. Maykop sought reassurance that no theft occurred during the Shuttered Lantern codification. A Great Library request remains unanswered.

n.Druj: Axou representatives of Grand Ilarch Dancia Terricos of Ipotavo remain committed to action against the Druj Tower of the Skink, and they hope to discuss a joint strategy for the Sarangrave war with the Military Council.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Apulian orc Batheka de Tassato Regario was an experienced Grendel commander before joining the League.
n.Highguard: More black-sailed Axou ships are arriving at Crown's Quay in Necropolis now that the Asavean bounty has ended, and trade is returning towards normal levels.
n.The Brass Coast: The Flame of Riqueza of the Brass Coast has succeeded Fintan Nighthaven as Ambassador to Axos. The new ambassador is expected to receive the Axou delegation in the Senate and to handle the coming Liberty Pact business.
n.The League: Axos proposed paying 5 thrones a season for its officers to study at the Five Cities Military Academy in Tassato, which would need a Senate motion to accept. The League's Batheka de Tassato Regario suggested casually inviting Axou siege commanders or toxatai captains so the Empire might learn from them.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the codified Oath of the Bleak Garden is believed to draw on work by the Urizen Spyridonakes of the Lighthouse-That-Was, and Axou battle-mages are compared to Urizen sentinels.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Mistress Isephenia of Maykop helps run the House of Spirits in Casinea alongside Bursar Rinnah.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Axou engineers are described as almost as skilled as those from Holberg.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is not named directly, and the only apparent link is the new Ambassador, The Flame of Riqueza of the Brass Coast.
t.Necropolis: Trade through Crown's Quay is recovering, with more black-sailed Axou ships arriving now that the Asavean bounty has ended and Imperial escorts continue.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the Oath of the Bleak Garden codified in Maykop is believed to be based on work by Spyridonakes of the Lighthouse-That-Was.
t.Sarangrave: Axos hopes to agree a joint strategy against the Druj Tower of the Skink in the Sarangrave. Representatives of Grand Ilarch Dancia Terricos remain committed to taking action there.
t.Tassato: Axou officers from Ipotavo, Kaban and Issyk wish to study at the Five Cities Military Academy and the Barossa School in Tassato. Their attendance would bring in 5 thrones a season but carries a risk of espionage, and it depends on the Senate approving it.

Upon a midnight dreary.d: Callidus offered to find Brass Coast founders' relics for a heavy price, and Basileia sent cryptic next steps in the plot against Salt Lord Seonag. Irra Harah threatened war if the Empire attacked the Nesustak rebels, while Arhallogen offered to slaughter them. Cathan Canae warned that a new territory must be conquered by Summer 388YE after Mieriada's cession. Knights of Glory armies in Sarangrave can no longer take cautious orders. Barien summoned Dawnish and Wintermark victors to judge glory against heroism. Skathe offered Catena help codifying a curse. Surut's Brand will stay in Necropolis if granted amity. Tharim's knights destroyed Agramant's covens in Upwold but badly damaged its farms and businesses.

n.Dawn: Dawnish challenge victors were summoned to Axmure to argue before Barien that glory surpasses heroism. Miners in Dawnish lands have suffered drowning nightmares that Jaheris's heralds claim they can turn to profit.
n.Druj: The Druj lost the Nesustak Forest to rebel slave septs backed by Irra Harah, though they kept Whisperwood. Skathe offered Catena help in codifying a curse to spread misery across Druj lands.
