n.Grendel: Overseer Hook reported that Salt Lord Seonag had hosted Broken Shore orcs calling for abolition, while Basileia's plot to assassinate her moved forward. Cathan Canae raised no objection to recognising the Protectorate of Mareave.
n.Highguard: Surut's Brand, around 1,000 burned knights, guarded Necropolis's coast for a season. They will stay until Spring 388YE only if the Conclave grants Surut amity.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae will not count retaking the Jotun-held lands of Bregasland and Liathaven as conquering a new territory.
n.Navarr: Ossegrahn withdrew his support from Greenwatch, so the Greenwatcher lost the Implements of Willowbraid. Arhallogen hinted it might deal with the Conclave, not only its Navarr allies, if its offer were taken up.
n.The Brass Coast: Callidus offered, at a steep price, to track down Erigo's gold-and-ruby circlet and Guerra's crimson sash. The Freeborn armies Fire of the South and Burning Falcon now share the Knights of Glory effect that bars cautious orders.
n.The League: Miners in League lands have reported drowning nightmares. Jaheris's heralds invited affected mine owners to the Plot and Plunder bar in the League camp to hear their scheme.
n.The Marches: Tharim's knights wiped out Agramant's covens in Upwold, but their brutal methods damaged farms and businesses across the territory. Alf Alwen and Jim Bribben were not found.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae cited the Empire's cession of Mieriada to the Thule as the kind of thing that angers her.
n.Urizen: Catena's Urizeni Assembly pledge to eradicate the Druj so pleased Skathe that the eternal offered to help her codify a curse of any realm and magnitude.
n.Varushka: Varushkan miners have suffered nightmares of drowning. Jaheris's heralds, who crossed Varushka from Miekarova, claim to know their source and a scheme to profit from it.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's victors were summoned to argue before Barien that heroism surpasses glory. Eleonaris praised the Voices of the Unbound Storm for their Knights of Glory enchantments.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the page does not discuss the Bay directly; its only link is indirect, through the knights watching Necropolis's coast against attack from the sea.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae will not count Bregasland as a new territory, as it was once Imperial.
t.Brocéliande: A Sentinel Gate conjunction opens to a strong Night regio here, which Lashonar's heralds urge be used to cast Nathair Autumngale's arcane projection. Ritualists would face only a minor risk of vallorn miasma.
t.Holberg: Holberg's mine owners were invited to hear Jaheris's heralds explain the drowning nightmares and their scheme to profit from them.
t.Karov: Karov's mine owners were invited to the Jaheris heralds' meeting about the subterranean nightmares and a plan to profit from them.
t.Karsk: Karsk's mine owners were among those invited to hear the Jaheris heralds' scheme about the miners' nightmares.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae will not count Liathaven as a new territory if it is retaken.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the recently recovered Madruga does not count as a new territory under Cathan Canae's terms.
t.Mareave: Cathan Canae confirmed that recognising the Protectorate of Mareave would not anger the Lady of the Frost.
t.Miekarova: Volstann cited the cession of Mieriada to the Thule as the kind of loss that angers Cathan Canae. Jaheris's heralds began their journey across Varushka from Miekarova.
t.Necropolis: Surut's Brand took up positions to defend Necropolis from attack by sea, worth around 1,000 troops. They will remain until Spring 388YE only if Surut is granted amity.
t.Ossium: Ossium's mine owners were invited to the Jaheris heralds' meeting about the miners' drowning nightmares.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the name appears only in a reference to Reumah's Redoubt as Necropolis's main coastal defence, not to this territory.
t.Sarangrave: Rebel septs backed by Irra Harah seized the Nesustak Forest, and Arhallogen offered to slaughter them. Imperial armies there enchanted with Knights of Glory can no longer take cautious orders.
t.Semmerholm: Barien's challenge finale will be held at the Grove of the Thousand in Axmure. Semmerholm's mine owners were also invited to the Jaheris heralds' meeting.
t.The Barrens: Mine owners in the Barrens were invited to the Jaheris heralds' meeting. The contested Nesustak Forest lies on the Barrens' border.
t.Therunin: Peakedge Stead was destroyed by the Druj and Ossegrahn turned away from the Empire, leaving an enchanted glade said to be untouched by the vallorn. Therunin also does not count as a new territory for Cathan Canae.
t.Upwold: Tharim's knights destroyed two Agramant covens and the Circle of Stone remnants. Their damage will cost every farm and business 36 rings at Winter, with Heart's Blood compensation possible if the Conclave approves.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz's mine owners were invited to the Jaheris heralds' meeting about the subterranean nightmares.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater's mine owners were invited to hear Jaheris's heralds explain the miners' nightmares and their money-making scheme.

r.Brocéliande/Vale's Lament: The Sentinel Gate opens to the Singing Circle, a strong Night regio here, where Lashonar hopes to see An Ode To Blood And Sacrifice cast.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Cathan Canae has no objection to the Empire recognising the city state of Beoraidh.
r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Its cession to the Thule prompted Volstann's warning that the Empire must conquer a new territory by the end of Summer 388YE.
r.Necropolis/Coursmouth: Surut's burned knights took up positions in Coursmouth to watch the coast.
r.Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand: Surut's Brand stationed itself in Sanctuary Sand to guard against attack from the sea.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The Bloodwater Spears, the Water Walkers and another sept overthrew the Druj here with Irra Harah's backing. Attacking them would be illegal and would bring Irra Harah's war, though Arhallogen offered to do it for the Empire.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: Mentioned in passing: if the Druj are forced out of Thornfen, the rebels might claim more of Sarangrave.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: The rebels tried and failed to take Whisperwood from the Druj. The Empire could still seize it by driving the Druj out.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: Barien's victors and their skops and troubadours gather at the Grove of the Thousand here to present their deeds.

Volumes of forgotten lore.d: A fifty-mana Night vision of Vesna crushing the Empire appeared over Casinea, and strange dreams returned there. Blackdamp proposed Nightfingers, a great work yielding deepstones for Varushkan mines. Thorns found the Three Stones regio in Therunin's Greenheart. The Woundbinder of the Mark was called to aid merchants attacked in Stark. The City of Gold and Lead refused potions and drugs, offered vis trades and advertised Callidus's auction. The Loom of Spells auction continued. The Conclave could request a new grand lodge proposal. Grateful Marchers gave a harvest bounty and gifts to titles. The Unfettered Mind gained the Well of Shadows, generals gained the Passionate Furlough order, and Spiral's dramatic strangeness persisted.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater is named as a place to which Blackdamp might later extend the Nightfingers bargain.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are blamed for destroying Therunin's trods when the Tainted Basilisk used blood magic to unleash the vallorn of Tharunind.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel invasion of southern Mareave is noted, as the Golden Pyramid grand lodge there was completed despite it.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Casinea saw the controversial vision of Empress Vesna and renewed unsettling dreams. Some Highborn and Casinean priests questioned whether such images amounted to idolatry and urged the Imperial Censor to act.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a territory to which Blackdamp might later extend its Nightfingers offer.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland, held by the Jotun that season, is the destination of aid caravans now avoiding Stark. Marcher magicians also fear what Rivers Run Red might do there.
n.Navarr: Thorns of the Sevencut striding found the Three Stones, a potent Spring regio in Therunin where Dance of Navarr and Thorn might be performed. Navarr messengers carried a flood of letters in the debate over Imperial enchantments.
n.The League: League citizens with resources in Spiral continued to experience dramatic magical strangeness and could draw on a dramaturgical persona, with Night magicians gaining extra ritual strength. The League was also noted as untouched by the Cold Sun incident.
n.The Marches: Marchers, angered by the attempt to license Rivers Run Red, gathered a 10-Throne harvest bounty for the Conclave to endow to anyone but the Rod and Shield. They sent gifts to several Marcher title holders and suggested the Senate amend those titles to make the gifts partly permanent.
n.Urizen: Urizen citizens with resources in Spiral shared in its dramatic phenomena and persona benefits. Urizen's Quick Study ritual was confirmed to work with the Loom of Spells.
n.Varushka: Blackdamp offered Varushka the Nightfingers, standing-stone great works costing 60 white granite and 15 mithril. Each would give every mine in its territory two deepstones a season. They could be built in Volodmartz, Karov, Miekarova or Karsk but not Ossium, and there were undisclosed further terms.
n.Wintermark: In Sermersuaq, aid caravans bound for Bregasland were shunning Stark's roads after attacks. A lost Atalaq expedition left wounded merchants whom Woundbinder of the Mark Conrald Mystrim was responsible for treating.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland is the destination of aid caravans avoiding Stark, and Marcher magicians fear for it should Rivers Run Red ever cease to be interdicted.
t.Casinea: A towering vision of Empress Vesna shattering a crystal Empire lit Casinea's sky, sparking debate over its meaning and its fifty-mana cost. Strange dreams of intrigue and battle returned to those sleeping there.
t.Karov: Karov, home of the Weeping Stone, is one of four territories where Blackdamp's proposed Nightfingers could be built to supply its mines with deepstones.
t.Karsk: Karsk is one of four territories where the proposed Nightfingers great work could be raised, giving each mine there two deepstones a season.
t.Mareave: The Grand Lodge of the Golden Pyramid was completed in Mareave despite the Grendel invasion in the south of the territory, opening the way for a new grand lodge proposal.
t.Miekarova: Blackdamp's messenger claimed to bring word from Miekarova, which is one of the four territories eligible for the Nightfingers.
t.Mitwold: Grateful Mitwold folk joined a harvest whip-round of food and drink, sold to fund a 10-Throne bounty for the Conclave to endow.
t.Mournwold: Lingering anger over Rivers Run Red's use in the scouring of the Mournwold fuelled Marcher hostility to the declaration. Its people joined the harvest whip-round in thanks that the interdiction stayed.
t.Ossium: Ossium was declared unsuitable for the Nightfingers, for reasons Blackdamp's messenger would not explain.
t.Sermersuaq: Rumours of wind-riding monsters made aid caravans avoid Stark's roads. A missing expedition carrying food for Sanna's Hall left wounded merchants in need of the Woundbinder of the Mark.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a possible future extension of the Nightfingers bargain.
t.Spiral: Spiral's magical tumult of drama, masks and strange phenomena intensified. League and Urizen residents could draw on dramaturgical personae, and Night magicians gained an extra effective rank.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar is named as a place Blackdamp might extend the Nightfingers to once one was built.
t.Therunin: Therunin's trods had been shattered by the Druj unleashing the vallorn. Thorns found the Three Stones regio, where the Archmage of Spring was responsible for supporting a casting of Dance of Navarr and Thorn.
t.Upwold: A herald of Sadogua took up semi-permanent residence in the woods near King's Stoke, ready to guide a member of the Unfettered Mind to the Well of Shadows each season.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz is one of four territories where the Nightfingers could be built to grant its mines deepstones each season.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater is suggested as a possible future beneficiary of the Nightfingers bargain.

r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Mentioned in passing: linked to the account of the lost aid expedition from Atalaq, whose wounded travellers the Woundbinder of the Mark was called to treat.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: Aid caravans for Bregasland avoided Stark's roads amid rumours of derailed wagons and wind-borne attackers. A missing expedition's survivors reported bandits hurling coins, led by a horned woman veined with ore.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Visitors to Apulus often found themselves lost in unfamiliar parts of the city, stumbling into dramatic productions and wild revelry.
r.Therunin/Greenheart: The Three Stones, a potent Spring regio sheltered by a weirwood grove against vallorn miasma and vallornspawn, was found in Greenheart as the best available site for Dance of Navarr and Thorn.
r.Upwold/Tower March: A herald of the eternal Sadogua settled in the woods near King's Stoke to escort a member of the Unfettered Mind to the Well of Shadows each season.
